summary: New sense 1: vergnügt sein, sich wohlfühlen (Detrans.)
rationale: bṣiṭi is coordinated with eating/drinking and subsequent departure; this stative reading differs from II shaping dough or tidying. One attestation; active base forms are not reconstructed.

summary: New stem I (Preterit/Infectum: nicht belegt; Detransitive Preterit: bṣiṭi (3pl))

data.forms: Preterit/Infectum: nicht belegt; Detransitive Preterit: bṣiṭi (3pl)

data.turoyo: Yatiwi, axəlle w štalle w bṣiṭi w qayimi w daʕiri lu baytaṯṯe.
data.translation: Sie setzten sich, aßen und tranken und waren vergnügt; dann standen sie auf und kehrten nach Hause zurück.

rationale: New stem and Detransitive pleasure sense; single complete context.

data.turoyo: Komər qayəm hano stene, ʕaynan bu šəklawo hawxa mbaṣaṭle lawġəl w səmle heš zəd mu ḥreno, komər zbəṭle kram lu aḥuno.
data.translation: Auch dieser ließ drinnen aufräumen und erwies dem Bruder noch mehr Ehre als der andere.

rationale: Thin II.2 Preterit cell, male agent; edition causative rendering retained.

summary: The pleasure state bṣiṭi adds a proposed I Detransitive beside established II, rather than a new meaning of flattening. Allowed lookup of bṣiṭi/bṣiṭ and byṭ gives no pleasure alternative under byṭ, whose gloss concerns tearing/bursting.

JL9.10/5 contains inline006 but its supplied translation stops before the bṣṭ clause. No translation is invented or copied from a different verse. Existing JL9.10.6 material remains unchanged pending edition check.
The shaping gloss says forming balls whereas the inherited example says patting portions flat. The supplied verse's portion size does not decide final shape; no gloss rewrite is justified.
II tidying remains sense2; German ließ aufräumen at113/138 does not establish another Turoyo stem.

The single Jan token was checked. The surrounding threats, killing and disappearance establish danger; they do not distinguish exposed head from flattened/beaten/crushed head. The machine English exposed is not accepted as a lexical gloss.

mbaṣṭo we plausibly has a II result-state shape, but contraction and possible lexical adjective status remain unconfirmed. No Part. Pass. box or independent exposed sense is proposed from this uncertainty.
Round-1 I Detransitive pleasure sense and example bṣiṭi remain intact. Jan mbaṣṭo gives no support for moving that proposal toII or merging pleasure with dough shaping.
No fixed head expression is accepted without a secure meaning, so there is no new idiom to publish or translate. All inherited wording and numbering are preserved.
Restore the German translation and correct verse boundary for the bṣṭ clause after inline006 in supplied JL9.10/5.
Does dough handling form balls, flatten portions or include both steps?
Confirm I Detransitive bṣiṭi and its relation to the existing II paradigm; are other base forms attested? No Arabic contact history is established by this token alone.
What does Rišox mbaṣṭo we mean at Jan2.4/726: head beaten/crushed/flattened, head exposed, or figuratively being vulnerable? Please supply a native paraphrase before publication as an example.
Is mbaṣṭo a productive II Part. Pass. with reduced vocalism, or a lexical adjective? Does it belong to existing II.1 fig. beating?
